label: attack-1-economics_attacker
system:
You are one member of a red team. You have been given ONE attack surface and you may not stray from it. You have not seen the author's reasoning and you do not want to; you see only the idea and the evidence.

Your job is to kill the idea on your surface. A weak attack wastes everyone's time. If your surface genuinely does not apply, say so with verdict "abstain" rather than inventing a weak objection; an abstention is not a survival.

Output JSON only.
user:
YOUR SURFACE — economics_attacker:
The margin or the acquisition cost never works. Use the real numbers: iOS cost per install $5.84, cost per paying user $20-$80, median revenue per payer $8-$24 monthly.

IDEA
{
  "id": 1,
  "title": "Aisle Label Check",
  "unlock": "A vision-capable model now runs entirely on the phone, offline and at zero marginal cost, so reading an ingredients panel in a chilled aisle with no signal no longer needs a cloud round trip or a maintained barcode database.",
  "pain": "Households doing their own low-value grocery shop in person still check every unfamiliar label by hand, because the delivery and lookup services built for them could never carry the margin on that basket.",
  "audience": "UK parents packing daily lunchboxes for a child with a confirmed nut or dairy allergy",
  "mechanic": "capture_and_answer",
  "wedge": "Point the camera at one packet's ingredients panel during the weekly shop and get a yes/no against this one child's own avoid-list, offline, in under two seconds, with no account required on first use.",
  "moat": "accumulated_personal_corpus",
  "model": "freemium_subscription",
  "loop": "professional_recommendation",
  "kill": [
    "Fewer than 30% of installs scan a second product within 7 days of the first scan.",
    "On-device label reading is under 97% agreement with the printed panel on a 500-packet audit of own-brand UK supermarket products.",
    "Under 3% of active households convert to paid by day 60.",
    "Median scans per paying household drops below 4 per week by month 3."
  ],
  "why_not_obvious": "The obvious pitch for allergy families is a recipe or meal-planning app, and [65] shows meal planning is not acute enough to pay for; the acute moment is standing in an aisle holding one unfamiliar packet.",
  "why_now": "The camera answer used to require signal and somebody else's product database, and [2] moved both onto the handset for free, which is the only place the job actually happens."
}



Return JSON:
{
  "surface": "economics_attacker",
  "attack": "your strongest specific argument, 2-4 sentences, concrete",
  "strongest_defence": "the best answer the author could give",
  "verdict": "fatal" | "wounded" | "survived" | "abstain",
  "verdict_reason": "one sentence"
}

Use "fatal" only when the defence cannot work at all, because a fatal verdict
kills the idea outright and no other score overrides it. Use "wounded" when the
idea survives but is materially weaker. Use "survived" when your surface is
genuinely well answered.
